header.note: Source: strings.json. Target locale: Spanish (es). Microsoft Language Portal consulted for approved Spanish gaming and UI terminology.

trans-unit.note:
CONTEXT: Full-screen overlay shown the instant the player clicks a mine and loses. Tone: Dramatic, punchy, exclamatory — mirrors the shock of the explosion. UI constraints: Short banner; prioritise impact over verbosity.
MICROSOFT TERMINOLOGY (via Microsoft Language Portal): - "Game Over" → approved Spanish equivalent is "Fin del juego", used across Xbox, Windows, and MSN Games including Microsoft's own Spanish Minesweeper localisation. - "BOOM" is an onomatopoeia. Microsoft retains "BOOM" for Latin American Spanish (es-419) and adapts to "¡BUM!" for Spain Spanish (es-ES). "BOOM" is used here as the universally understood form across all Spanish locales.
TRANSLATION RATIONALE: "¡BOOM! ¡Fin del juego!" Aligns with Microsoft's approved term; retains "BOOM" for cross-regional intelligibility. If targeting es-ES exclusively, consider "¡BUM! ¡Fin del juego!".

CONTEXT: Full-screen overlay shown when the player successfully clears the board. Tone: Celebratory, triumphant. All-caps in the source to convey excitement. UI constraints: Short banner; mirror the energy and register of the English source.
MICROSOFT TERMINOLOGY (via Microsoft Language Portal): - "You Win" / "You Won" → approved Spanish equivalent is "¡Has ganado!" (present perfect, second-person singular informal), used in MSN Games, Xbox achievements, and the official Solitaire/Minesweeper localisations. - All-caps ("¡HAS GANADO!") matches the source register and is standard in Microsoft's Spanish game UI strings. - Regional note: "¡GANASTE!" (preterite) is more natural in Latin American Spanish (es-419) and equally valid if targeting es-MX or es-419.
TRANSLATION RATIONALE: "¡HAS GANADO!" Matches Microsoft's approved gaming terminology and preserves the all-caps source register. If targeting es-419, consider "¡GANASTE!" instead.
